summary: myidsan had ZERO screen checks - every bench it has ever had was an API bench - so the first one (tools/fleetbench/uicheck_idsan_admin.js) drives all twelve admin sections in headless Chrome, in all four languages, and then drives real workflows and confirms the SERVER changed. It found two real defects, both invisible from the API side. First and worse: a 401 did not return the SPA to the sign-in screen. apiRequest threw on any non-OK response and every page caught it like an ordinary error and rendered its own empty state, so an operator whose session had ended - expired, revoked by an administrator, or ended by themselves from the Users page, which includes their own row - was left sitting in a fully drawn admin console with a small red 'session not active' and the Audit log announcing 'No events match these filters'. The screen was lying, and only the screenshot showed it. api.js now announces a lost session on 401 (and deliberately NOT on 403, which is 'you are signed in and may not do this' and is also how the step-up sentinel arrives), and App.js returns to the sign-in screen; the announcement fires at most once per lost session so a page fanning out parallel requests cannot bounce the operator several times, and a new sign-in re-arms it. Second: the Users page offers 'End all sessions' on every row INCLUDING the operator's own, and the confirmation said 'End every session for this account? They will have to sign in again' - wording that quietly assumed somebody else. Pressing it on your own row signs you out immediately, which is a legitimate emergency action but not what that sentence describes. A separate self-worded confirmation now says so, in all four languages. The check itself also proves, per language, that every section renders with a heading, leaks no untranslated dictionary key, and that every enabled control is HIT-TESTABLE at its own centre (document.elementFromPoint at the control's own midpoint - the test that once found a button which rendered perfectly and could not be pressed, in Arabic only); and it exercises create AND DELETE on Roles, because a green run that never deletes has not covered delete. 21/21 in English, 8/8 ms, 8/8 zh, 9/9 ar against the fix; 19/21 against unfixed main on the same English checks.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; frontend only, no API, schema or configuration change. The visible difference is that a session which ends underneath an operator now returns them to the sign-in screen instead of leaving them in an admin console where every page reports no data - so an operator who had learned to read 'No events match these filters' as 'the audit log is broken' will now simply be asked to sign in again. A 403 still surfaces inline on the page exactly as before, which is what keeps the step-up re-authentication prompt working. The 'End all sessions' button is unchanged in what it does; only the confirmation wording differs, and only on your own row.
